'''Alec Burks''' (born July 20, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Miami Heat]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] as the 12th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. Burks primarily plays the [[shooting guard]] position.

He played for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball]] team during his college years and was most notably the school's first-ever [[Big 12 Conference]] Freshman of the Year in 2010. As a sophomore, Burks was statistically the eighteenth-best scorer in the [[NCAA|Division I]]. With Colorado, he missed only a single college game. Burks also gained national attention after being selected to the Big 12 First Team in his second season with the Buffaloes. He entered the [[2011 NBA draft]] shortly after his sophomore year, projected to be a first-round draft pick despite playing just two seasons at Colorado.

==High school career==
Burks attended Grandview High School, where in 2009 he was named the [[Gatorade Player of the Year]] in the state of Missouri. As a senior, he averaged 23.0 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.6 steals per game. He was also named the [[Kansas City Star]] and Metro Sports Player of the Year during his senior year.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.cubuffs.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=204798841|title=Alec Burks Bio|work=CUBuffs.com|access-date=November 6, 2011}}</ref>

Prior to his senior year of high school, Burks signed with Colorado during the November 2008 signing period.<ref name="bio" />

Considered a three-star recruit by [[247Sports.com]], Burks was listed as the No. 49 shooting guard and the No. 196 player in the nation in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Alec-Burks-59632?Institution=14476|title=Alec Burks Recruiting Profile|work=247Sports.com|access-date=June 23, 2011}}</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman year at [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]], Burks was awarded the 2010 Big 12 Conference Freshman of the Year, while also being named in the Big 12 All-Rookie team.<ref name="bio" />

In his sophomore year, he was named in the All-Big 12 first team.<ref name="bio" />

In April 2011, Burks decided to forgo his two remaining eligible college years to enter the NBA draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cubuffs.com/sports/2011/4/21/205140897.aspx|title=Alec Burks To Enter NBA Draft|work=CUBuffs.com|date=April 21, 2011|access-date=January 9, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Utah Jazz (2011–2018)===
Burks was selected with the 12th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz_selects_kanter_and_burks.html|title=Jazz Selects Enes Kanter and Alec Burks in 2011 NBA Draft|work=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2011|access-date=June 23, 2011}}</ref> On December 9, 2011, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz_sign_kanter_and_burks.html|title=Jazz Signs 2011 Lottery Picks|work=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2011|access-date=December 9, 2011}}</ref> On October 25, 2012, the Jazz exercised their third-year team option on Burks' rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-exercises-team-options-four-players.html|title=Jazz Exercises Team Options on Four Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2012|access-date=October 25, 2012}}</ref> On October 29, 2013, the Jazz exercised their fourth-year team option on Burks' rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-exercises-team-options-burks-and-kanter|title=Jazz Exercises Team Options on Burks and Kanter|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2013|access-date=October 29, 2013}}</ref>

On January 13, 2014, Burks scored a career-high 34 points in a 118–103 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Payne|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140113/DENUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Jazz 118, Nuggets 103|work=NBA.com|date=January 14, 2014|access-date=January 14, 2014}}</ref>

On October 31, 2014, Burks signed a four-year, $42 million contract extension with the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Lea|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-alec-burks-multi-year-contract-extension|title=Jazz Sign Alec Burks to Multi-Year Contract Extension|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2014|access-date=October 31, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Windhorst|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11796613/alec-burks-agrees-4-year-42-million-extension-utah-jazz|title=Alec Burks gets 4-year extension|work=ESPN.com|date=November 1, 2014|access-date=November 1, 2014}}</ref> On December 30, he was ruled out for the rest of the 2014–15 season due to a shoulder injury.<ref>{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Lea|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/alec-burks-injury-update-december-30-2014|title=Alec Burks Injury Update – December 30, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2014|access-date=December 30, 2014}}</ref>

On December 27, 2015, Burks was ruled out for six weeks with an ankle fracture.<ref>{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--jazz-s-alec-burks-sidelined-at-least-six-weeks-203840269.html|title=Sources: Jazz's Alec Burks sidelined at least six weeks|work=Yahoo.com|date=December 27, 2015|access-date=December 27, 2015}}</ref> Two days later, he elected to undergo surgery on his fractured left fibula.<ref>{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--alec-burks-to-have-surgery-on-fractured-fibula-032000777.html|title=Sources: Jazz's Alec Burks to have surgery on fractured fibula|work=Yahoo.com|date=December 29, 2015|access-date=December 29, 2015}}</ref> On April 8, 2016, he returned to action after missing 50 games with the injury. In 13 minutes off the bench, he scored 11 points on 4-of-5 shooting in a 102–99 overtime loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=John|last=Coon|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160408/LACUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Crawford scores 30, including winner to lead Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=April 9, 2016|access-date=April 9, 2016}}</ref>

On November 30, 2017, Burks scored a season-high 28 points off the bench in a 126–107 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975068|title=Jazz overwhelm Clippers in fourth to win 126-107|work=ESPN.com|date=November 30, 2017|access-date=December 1, 2017}}</ref> On December 4, 2017, he scored 27 points in a 116–69 win over the [[Washington Wizards]] for his third straight game with 20 or more—his best string since three straight 20-point games in February 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975100|title=Burks scores 27, Jazz run away from Wizards 116-69|work=ESPN.com|date=December 4, 2017|access-date=December 4, 2017}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018–2019)===
On November 29, 2018, Burks was traded, along with two future second-round picks, to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Kyle Korver]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/burks-trade-181129|title=Cavaliers Acquire Alec Burks and Two Future Second Round Picks from Utah|work=NBA.com|date=November 29, 2018|access-date=November 29, 2018}}</ref> Burks made his Cavaliers debut the next day, recording 15 points, six rebounds, four assists and two steals in a 128–95 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Cavaliers vs Boston Celtics Nov 30, 2018 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021800319 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 3, he made a game-winning dunk with 3.2 seconds left to give the Cavaliers a 99–97 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alec Burks' late dunk seals Cleveland Cavs' 99-97 win over slumping Brooklyn Nets |url=https://www.wkyc.com/article/sports/nba/cavaliers/alec-burks-late-dunk-seals-cleveland-cavs-99-97-win-over-slumping-brooklyn-nets/95-620531540 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=WKYC |date=December 3, 2018 }}</ref> He also had 13 points and seven rebounds in the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Cavaliers vs Brooklyn Nets Dec 3, 2018 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021800345 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 7, Burks tied his season high of 22 points, alongside seven rebounds and a season-high nine assists, in a 129–110 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sacramento Kings vs Cleveland Cavaliers Dec 7, 2018 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021800372 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 13, 2019, he had 17 points and a season-high 13 rebounds in a 101–95 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071320|title=Cavs stun Lakers 101-95 to end 12-game losing streak|work=ESPN.com|date=January 13, 2019|access-date=January 13, 2019}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2019)===
On February 7, 2019, Burks was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/knight-chriss-trade-190207|title=Cavs Acquire Brandon Knight, Marquese Chriss Plus Picks in Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2019|access-date=February 7, 2019}}</ref> He made his Kings debut a day later, recording nine points and four rebounds in a 102–96 win over the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Heat vs Sacramento Kings Feb 8, 2019 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021800824 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors (2019–2020)===
On July 11, 2019, Burks signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/alec-burks-signing-20190711|title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Guard Alec Burks|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2019}}</ref> He made his Warriors debut on October 30, recording seven points and two assists in a 121–110 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CURRY BREAKS LEFT HAND IN ANOTHER EMBARRASSING WARRIORS LOSS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900065 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 20, 2020, Burks scored a season-high 33 points, alongside seven rebounds, eight assists and three blocks, in a 129–124 overtime loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=LILLARD SCORES 61 AND BLAZERS BEAT WARRIORS 129-124 IN OT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900652 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 30, he switched his jersey number from 8 to 20 out of respect for the late [[Kobe Bryant]], who died in a helicopter crash four days earlier.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/alec-burks-changes-jersey-20200130|title=Alec Burks Changes Jersey Number "Out of Respect" for the Late Kobe Bryant Warriors wing joins a growing list of players who will no longer wear No. 8 or 24|date=January 30, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 30, 2020}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2020)===
On February 6, 2020, Burks was traded, alongside [[Glenn Robinson III]], to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for three future second-round picks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/team-acquires-burks-robinson-iii|title=Team Acquires Burks, Robinson III|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2020}}</ref> Burks made his 76ers debut on February 11, recording two points and two assists in a 110–103 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=RICHARDSON, SIMMONS LEAD 76ERS PAST CLIPPERS 110-103 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900802 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The 76ers faced the [[Boston Celtics]] during their first round playoff series, but they were eliminated in a four-game sweep.

===New York Knicks (2020–2022)===
On November 22, 2020, Burks signed a one-year, $6 million contract with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks Sign Alec Burks |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-alec-burks |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 22, 2020 |date=November 22, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Miranda | first=Matthew | title=Knicks re-sign Alec Burks to 3 yr/$30M deal | website=Posting and Toasting|publisher=SB Nation | date=2021-08-02 | url=https://www.postingandtoasting.com/2021/8/2/22606686/knicks-re-sign-alec-burks-to-3-yr-30m-deal | access-date=2025-12-11}}</ref> He made his Knicks debut on December 23, recording 22 points, four rebounds and three assists in a 121–107 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=SABONIS, OLADIPO LEAD PACERS PAST KNICKS ON OPENING NIGHT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000011 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On May 13, 2021, Burks scored a season-high 30 points, alongside ten rebounds and two assists, in a 102–98 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BURKS SCORES 30, RALLIES KNICKS PAST SPURS, 102-98 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000458 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He helped the Knicks qualify for the playoffs for the first time since [[2013 NBA playoffs|2013]], and they faced the [[Atlanta Hawks]] during their first-round series. On May 23, Burks recorded 27 points, three rebounds and four assists in a 107–105 Game 1 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=YOUNG HITS RUNNER WITH 0.9 LEFT TO LIFT HAWKS PAST KNICKS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000131 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Knicks ended up losing the series in five games.

On August 18, 2021, Burks re-signed with the Knicks on a three-year, $30 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Knicks Re-Sign Alec Burks |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-re-sign-alec-burks |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Knicks re-sign Alec Burks to 3 yr/$30M deal |url=https://www.postingandtoasting.com/2021/8/2/22606686/knicks-re-sign-alec-burks-to-3-yr-30m-deal |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=SB Nation |date=August 2, 2021 }}</ref> On December 29, he scored a career-high 34 points, alongside four rebounds, two assists and three steals, in a 94–85 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BURKS, KNICKS BENCH POWER PAST SHORT-HANDED PISTONS 94-85 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100516 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Knicks failed to qualify for the playoffs during the 2021–22 season, finishing with a 37–45 record.

===Detroit Pistons (2022–2024)===
On July 11, 2022, Burks was traded, alongside [[Nerlens Noel]], to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Nikola Radičević]] and a 2025 protected second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS ACQUIRE ALEC BURKS, NERLENS NOEL, DRAFT PICKS AND CASH CONSIDERATIONS|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-alec-burks-nerlens-noel-draft-picks-and-cash-considerations|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2022|access-date=July 11, 2022}}</ref> Burks made his Pistons debut on November 11, recording 17 points and two rebounds in a 121–112 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NEW YORK KNICKS HOLD ON FOR 121-112 WIN OVER DETROIT PISTONS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200178 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On June 29, 2023, the [[Detroit Pistons]] exercised Burks' team option for the [[2023–24 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|number=1674483862863224840|title=The Detroit Pistons have picked up its team options for Isaiah Livers, Alec Burks and Eugene Omoruyi for the 2023-24 season.|user=Pistons_PR|date=June 29, 2023|access-date=August 2, 2023}}</ref> On January 16, 2024, Burks tied a career–high in points, registering 34 points while going 11–for–17 on field goals against the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref name="t328">{{cite web | title=Pistons' Alec Burks: Ties career high with 34 points | website=CBSSports.com | date=2024-01-16 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-alec-burks-ties-career-high-with-34-points/amp/ | access-date=2024-12-23}}</ref>

===Return to the Knicks (2024)===
On February 8, 2024, Burks and [[Bojan Bogdanović]] were traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Ryan Arcidiacono]], [[Malachi Flynn]], [[Evan Fournier]], [[Quentin Grimes]] and two second-round picks.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Acquire Bojan Bogdanovic and Alec Burks|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-acquire-bojan-bogdanovic-and-alec-burks|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Tim|last=Bontemps|title=Pistons trade Bojan Bogdanovic, Alec Burks to Knicks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39484645/sources-pistons-finalizing-trade-alec-burks-knicks|website=ESPN.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2024–2025)===
On July 4, 2024, Burks signed with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN ALEC BURKS|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-alec-burks|website=NBA.com|date=July 4, 2024|access-date=July 4, 2024}}</ref>
